answer: Sequential work registry: each identity must complete a random, verifiable task chain before it can transact, and chains are keyed to a shared clock so no identity can advance before the prior dawn's assignments finalize. Cloning forces attackers to redo every step in sequence, paying full compute and latency per clone as costs spiral. The chain seeds from a basalt-derived randomness beacon, so precomputation fails. Honest agents finish one chain; attackers pay N times the serial work for N identities.
